title: Static Files and Caching
description: Learn to serve static assets efficiently in ASP.NET Core using UseStaticFiles, configure cache headers for browser and CDN caching, and implement response caching for dynamic content.

blocks.text: Serving Static Files

Static files are client-side assets like CSS stylesheets, JavaScript bundles, images, and fonts. By default, ASP.NET Core serves these files from the wwwroot folder in your project. The UseStaticFiles middleware is what makes this possible — without it, requests for static assets return 404 errors.

Static files are served directly by the web server without going through the MVC or Razor Pages pipeline. This makes them extremely fast to serve and is one reason ASP.NET Core performs so well for both dynamic and static content.
Default Static File Configuration
The simplest way to enable static files is to call app.UseStaticFiles() with no parameters. This serves files from wwwroot with default options, including no cache headers.

blocks.title: Basic static file configuration
blocks.content: Enable static file serving with default options.

blocks.text: With this configuration, a file at wwwroot/css/site.css is accessible at the URL '/css/site.css'. The middleware maps the URL path directly to the file system path under wwwroot.
Any file placed in wwwroot is publicly accessible by default. Never store secrets, configuration files, or sensitive data in wwwroot. Files in this folder are meant to be served directly to clients.
Setting Cache-Control Headers

Browser caching reduces load times for repeat visitors and reduces bandwidth costs. You control caching behavior through HTTP cache headers, primarily the Cache-Control header. Static files that rarely change — like hashed CSS bundles and versioned JavaScript — should be cached aggressively.

blocks.title: Configuring cache headers for static files
blocks.content: Set a long cache duration for static assets using StaticFileOptions.

blocks.text: The Cache-Control header 'public,max-age=31536000' tells browsers and CDNs that this response can be cached for one year. When you need to force an update, use cache busting techniques like appending a content hash to the filename, for example 'site.abc123.css'. The URL changes when the content changes, so browsers fetch the new file.

blocks.title: Tip: Use content hashes for cache busting
blocks.text: Bundlers and build tools like Webpack, Vite, or Gulp can append a hash based on file content to filenames. When the file changes, the hash changes, producing a new URL that bypasses the cache.
Serving Files from Multiple Locations

You can serve static files from multiple directories by adding additional StaticFileOptions with custom FileProvider instances. This is useful when you need to serve user-uploaded files or files managed by another system.

blocks.title: Serving files from a custom directory
blocks.content: Configure a second static file source for user uploads at the '/uploads' URL path.

blocks.text: The PhysicalFileProvider points the middleware at the custom directory, and RequestPath defines the URL prefix. A request to '/uploads/report.pdf' will serve the file from 'UserUploads/report.pdf' on disk.
Response Caching for Dynamic Content

For dynamic content generated by controllers or Razor Pages, you can use the Response Caching Middleware. Unlike static file caching, response caching stores the full HTTP response — headers and body — so the middleware can return a cached copy without hitting your controller code.
Response caching is controlled by HTTP cache headers like Cache-Control on both the server and client. The middleware respects these headers to determine what can be cached and for how long.
Configuring Response Caching
To enable response caching, register the service and add the middleware. Controllers and pages then opt into caching by setting cache profiles or decorating actions with cache attributes.

blocks.title: Enabling response caching with a cache profile
blocks.content: Configure response caching services and a cache profile, then apply it to a controller.

blocks.title: Important: Response caching requires Vary headers
blocks.text: If your response varies based on query parameters, headers, or user identity, make sure to set the Vary response header accordingly. Without proper Vary headers, the response cache might serve the wrong content to different users.

terms.definition: Middleware that serves static files from the file system, typically the wwwroot folder.
Configuration options for UseStaticFiles, including OnPrepareResponse for custom headers and alternate FileProviders.
An HTTP response header that specifies browser and CDN caching directives like max-age and public.
Middleware that caches full HTTP responses in server memory to avoid re-executing controller logic.
A technique that changes a resource URL (usually via content hash) to force browsers to fetch an updated file.

blocks.title: Vary header for response caching
blocks.content: Ensure cached responses vary correctly when query parameters affect the output.

blocks.title: Configure Static Files and Response Caching
blocks.description: Set up static file serving with cache headers and add response caching to a dynamic controller action.
steps: Create a new MVC project: 'dotnet new mvc -n StaticCachingDemo'
Add a 'products.jpg' image to wwwroot/images and a 'site.css' file to wwwroot/css
Configure UseStaticFiles with OnPrepareResponse to set Cache-Control to 'public,max-age=86400' (1 day)
Register AddResponseCaching in the service collection and add app.UseResponseCaching() to the pipeline
Add a ProductsController with a GetFeatured action decorated with [ResponseCache(Duration = 30)]
Add a new cache profile named 'ProductsCache' with a 60-second duration
Run the app, verify that navigating to /images/products.jpg returns a Cache-Control header, and use curl -I to confirm the header is present
blocks.expectedOutcome: Static file requests return with a Cache-Control header showing max-age=86400. The dynamic GetFeatured action is cached for 30 seconds, verified by repeated requests returning the same response without controller execution.

items.hint: Use [ResponseCache] with Duration, CacheProfileName, and VaryByQueryKeys.

blocks.title: Static Files and Caching Summary
points: UseStaticFiles serves static assets from wwwroot or custom directories via FileProvider
Cache-Control headers control how long browsers and CDNs cache static files
Long cache durations paired with content-hash filenames provide optimal performance
Response Caching Middleware caches full HTTP responses from dynamic endpoints
Cache profiles centralize caching configuration for reuse across controllers
Always set Vary headers when cached responses depend on query parameters or user data
blocks.takeaway: Properly configured static file serving and caching dramatically improve application performance by reducing server load and response times. Combining long-lived static file caching with short-lived response caching for dynamic content provides the best user experience.
